questions.question: The three laws of thought include all of the following except:

options.D: The Law of the Excluded Middle

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a valid argument?

options.A: An argument where the premises and conclusion are all true
options.B: An argument where the premises logically lead to the conclusion
options.C: An argument that uses persuasive language
options.D: An argument that is widely accepted

questions.question: Which type of logic focuses on the structure of reasoning rather than the truth of the premises?
What is the key feature of a deductive argument?

options.A: It moves from specific cases to general principles
options.B: Its conclusion is only probable, not certain
options.C: If the premises are true, the conclusion must be true
options.D: It relies on examples and observation

questions.question: What distinguishes material logic from formal logic?

options.A: Material logic focuses on the truth of premises, while formal logic focuses on structure
options.B: Formal logic is concerned with argument content, while material logic checks validity
options.C: Material logic uses mathematical formulas, while formal logic does not
options.D: There is no difference between the two

questions.question: If an argument is valid but has false premises, what can be said about it?

options.C: It is neither valid nor invalid
options.D: The conclusion must also be false

questions.question: The statement 'If it is raining, then the ground is wet' is an example of:
What makes an argument sound?

options.A: The premises and conclusion are both true, regardless of validity
options.C: The argument is valid, and all premises are true

questions.question: What is the purpose of informal logic?

options.A: To analyze the structure of arguments without considering their truth
options.B: To study reasoning in everyday language and practical situations
options.C: To ensure that all arguments follow strict rules of inference
options.D: To examine only mathematical and symbolic reasoning

questions.question: The Law of the Excluded Middle states that:

options.A: Every statement must be either true or false, with no middle ground
options.B: Two contradictory statements can both be true under certain conditions
options.C: The structure of an argument is more important than its content
options.D: A statement can be both true and false at the same time

questions.question: True or False: Every valid argument must have a true conclusion.
True or False: The Law of Non-Contradiction states that a statement cannot be both true and false at the same time.
True or False: An argument can be valid even if one or more of its premises are false.
True or False: Material logic focuses on the structure of an argument rather than the truth of its premises.
True or False: If an argument is valid and has all true premises, then it is considered sound.
True or False: A compound statement is always an argument.
True or False: Deductive reasoning moves from general principles to specific conclusions.
True or False: Informal logic is used mainly in mathematical proofs and symbolic reasoning.
True or False: The Law of Identity states that 'A is A,' meaning that everything is itself.
True or False: If the conclusion of an argument is false, then at least one of the premises must also be false.
'All mammals are warm-blooded. Whales are mammals. Therefore, whales are warm-blooded.' Which option correctly identifies the conclusion?
'In order to pass the test, you must study hard. John did not study hard. Therefore, John will not pass the test.' What is the conclusion?

options.A: You must study hard to pass the test.
options.C: John will not pass the test.
options.D: Both A and B support the conclusion.

questions.question: 'All fruits have seeds. An apple is a fruit. Therefore, an apple has seeds.' Identify the premise(s) and the conclusion.

options.A: Premises: All fruits have seeds; Apple is a fruit. Conclusion: Apple has seeds.
options.B: Premise: Apple has seeds; Conclusion: All fruits have seeds.
options.C: Premise: Apple has seeds; Conclusion: Apple is a fruit.
options.D: Premises: All fruits have seeds; Apple has seeds. Conclusion: Apple is a fruit.

questions.question: 'Every student in the class passed the exam. Mary is a student in the class. Therefore, Mary passed the exam.' Which part is the conclusion?

options.A: Every student in the class passed the exam.
options.B: Mary is a student in the class.

questions.question: 'To win the game, you must practice regularly. Tom practices regularly. Therefore, Tom will win the game.' What are the premises and what is the conclusion?

options.A: Premises: You must practice regularly; Tom practices regularly. Conclusion: Tom will win the game.
options.B: Premise: Tom will win the game. Conclusion: Tom practices regularly.
options.C: Premises: Tom practices regularly; Tom will win the game. Conclusion: You must practice regularly.
options.D: Premise: To win the game, you must practice regularly. Conclusion: Tom practices regularly.

questions.question: 'If it is raining, then the picnic will be canceled. It is raining. Therefore, the picnic will be canceled.' Identify the conclusion.

options.A: If it is raining, then the picnic will be canceled.

questions.question: 'All dogs bark. Rex is a dog. Therefore, Rex barks.' Which option shows the premises and the conclusion?

options.A: Premise: All dogs bark. Conclusion: Rex is a dog.
options.B: Premises: All dogs bark; Rex is a dog. Conclusion: Rex barks.
options.C: Premise: Rex barks. Conclusion: All dogs bark and Rex is a dog.
options.D: Premise: Rex is a dog. Conclusion: All dogs bark.

questions.question: 'Studying daily improves your grades. Lisa studies daily. Therefore, Lisa's grades improve.' What is the conclusion?
'If you water plants, they grow. The garden was watered. Therefore, the plants grew.' Select the correct identification:

options.A: Premise: If you water plants, they grow; Garden was watered. Conclusion: Plants grew.
options.B: Premise: Plants grew; Conclusion: Garden was watered.
options.C: Premise: Garden was watered; Conclusion: If you water plants, they grow.
options.D: Premise: If you water plants, they grow; Conclusion: Garden was watered.

questions.question: 'Everyone who studies passes the exam. Alex did not study. Therefore, Alex will not pass the exam.' Identify the conclusion.

options.A: Everyone who studies passes the exam.
options.C: Alex will not pass the exam.
options.D: The argument has no clear conclusion.

options.D: Sound if the conclusion is true

'All computers run on electricity. My laptop is a computer. Therefore, my laptop runs on electricity.' This argument is:

options.D: Sound only if my laptop is plugged in

questions.question: 'Only mammals have fur. A dolphin is a mammal. Therefore, a dolphin has fur.' This argument is:
'If you exercise regularly, you will be healthy. You exercise regularly. Therefore, you are healthy.' This argument is:

options.D: Sound only if no other factors affect health

questions.question: 'All fish can fly. Goldie is a fish. Therefore, Goldie can fly.' Which premise is problematic?
'Every bird lays eggs. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins lay eggs.' Which premise might be challenged if we consider an exception?
'All planets are round, and Earth is a planet, then Earth is round.' Which premise could be disputed in certain philosophical discussions?
'All vehicles have four wheels. My motorcycle is a vehicle. Therefore, my motorcycle has four wheels.' Which premise is untrue?

'Every computer program is written in a high-level language. This software is a computer program. Therefore, this software is written in a high-level language.' If some programs are written in assembly language, which premise might be false?

options.A: Every computer program is written in a high-level language
options.B: This software is a computer program
options.C: This software is written in a high-level language

questions.question: 'If a person is a millionaire, then they are happy. John is not happy. Therefore, John is not a millionaire.' Which premise is likely questionable?

options.A: If a person is a millionaire, then they are happy

questions.question: 'All fruits are sweet. Lemons are fruits. Therefore, lemons are sweet.' Which premise is problematic?
'If a car is new, then it runs smoothly. This car is new. Therefore, it runs smoothly.' If the car has a manufacturing defect, which element is misleading?

options.A: If a car is new, then it runs smoothly

questions.question: 'Every student who studies passes the exam. Emily is a student. Emily passed the exam.' Which premise might be considered unverified if not every student who studies necessarily passes?

options.A: Every student who studies passes the exam

questions.question: 'If it rains, the streets get wet. The streets are wet. Therefore, it rained.' Which premise or assumption is problematic?

options.A: If it rains, the streets get wet
options.D: The argument wrongly assumes no other cause for wet streets.

questions.question: Identify the inductive argument:

options.A: If it rains, the ground gets wet. It rained. Therefore, the ground is wet.
options.B: All squares have four sides. A rectangle is a square. Therefore, a rectangle has four sides.
options.C: Most dogs bark when they see strangers. My neighbor's dog is barking. Therefore, it probably sees a stranger.
options.D: If an animal is a bird, it must lay eggs. A parrot is a bird. Therefore, it lays eggs.

questions.question: Which argument is deductive?

options.A: The last five times I drank coffee, I felt more awake. Therefore, drinking coffee always makes people more awake.
options.B: Every prime number greater than 2 is odd. 13 is a prime number greater than 2. Therefore, 13 is odd.
options.C: All swans I've seen are white. Therefore, all swans must be white.
options.D: The majority of past presidents have been male. Therefore, the next president will likely be male.

questions.question: Identify the inductive argument:

options.A: If it is raining, then the streets will be wet. It is raining. Therefore, the streets are wet.
options.B: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. A rocket engine pushes down, so the rocket moves up.
options.C: All cars I have ever seen have four wheels. Therefore, all cars must have four wheels.
options.D: Every bachelor is an unmarried man. John is a bachelor. Therefore, John is unmarried.

questions.question: Which of the following is deductive?

options.A: Most cats are independent. My friend has a cat. Therefore, my friend's cat is probably independent.
options.B: Every person who studies hard passes the exam. Mary studied hard. Therefore, Mary passed the exam.
options.C: The past five winters have been colder than average. Therefore, next winter will likely be colder than average.
options.D: 90% of the students in this school have smartphones. John is a student here, so he probably has a smartphone.

questions.question: Which argument is inductive?

options.A: No triangles have four sides. Shape X is a triangle. Therefore, shape X does not have four sides.
options.B: All people born in Canada are Canadian citizens. Sarah was born in Canada. Therefore, Sarah is a Canadian citizen.
options.C: Every swan I have seen is white. Therefore, the next swan I see will probably be white.
options.D: If an animal is a fish, then it breathes through gills. A shark is a fish. Therefore, it breathes through gills.

questions.question: What makes an argument deductive?

options.A: It draws conclusions based on probability and past experience.
options.B: It guarantees the truth of the conclusion if the premises are true.
options.C: It makes a generalization based on specific observations.
options.D: It assumes that the past will always predict the future.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of inductive reasoning?

options.A: All birds have feathers. A robin is a bird. Therefore, a robin has feathers.
options.B: No human can survive without oxygen. John is a human. Therefore, John needs oxygen to live.
options.C: My grandfather smoked and lived to 95. Therefore, smoking does not always cause early death.
options.D: If today is Tuesday, then tomorrow is Wednesday. Today is Tuesday. Therefore, tomorrow is Wednesday.

questions.question: A deductive argument is one in which:

options.A: The conclusion follows with certainty if the premises are true.
options.B: The conclusion is always true, even if the premises are false.
options.C: The conclusion is only probable, not certain.
options.D: The argument is based entirely on past observations.

questions.question: Which of the following best represents inductive reasoning?

options.A: All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Therefore, Socrates is mortal.
options.B: The last five times I went jogging, I felt great afterward. Therefore, jogging always makes people feel great.
options.C: If a shape is a square, then it has four equal sides. Shape X is a square. Therefore, it has four equal sides.
options.D: If a student studies, they pass the test. Mike studied. Therefore, he passed the test.
